name: אֱדוֹם
summary: The second name of Esau, Isaac’s firstborn and Jacob’s twin, and the name of the people descended from him and of their land, the hill country of Seir south of the Salt Sea. Scripture gives the reason: Esau came in faint from the field and said, “let me gulp some of the red, this red” (הָאָדֹם הָאָדֹם הַזֶּה), and sold his birthright for it; “therefore his name was called אֱדוֹם” (Gen 25:30). The name is the adjective אָדֹם, “red”, with other vowels; he had also come from the womb אַדְמוֹנִי, “red” (Gen 25:25). “Esau, he is Edom” (Gen 36:1, 8), and Israel is told, “you shall not abhor an Edomite (אֲדֹמִי), for he is your brother” (Deu 23:8). Most of the name’s hundred uses are of the nation and the land, which refused Israel passage, was subdued by David, and is judged by the prophets.

evidence.note: “Esau said to Jacob, Let me gulp, please, some of הָאָדֹם הָאָדֹם הַזֶּה, for I am faint; therefore his name was called אֱדוֹם.”
“The first came out אַדְמוֹנִי, all of him like a cloak of hair, and they called his name Esau.”
The red dish was bread and lentil stew; “so Esau despised the birthright”.
“These are the generations of Esau; he is אֱדוֹם.” So Gen 36:8, 19.
“Esau dwelt in the hill country of Seir; Esau, he is Edom”; “Esau, the father of אֱדוֹם”, the people.
“These are the chiefs of אֱדוֹם … he is Esau, the father of Edom.”
Jacob sent messengers to Esau “to the land of Seir, the field of אֱדוֹם”.
Moses to the king of Edom: “Thus says your brother Israel”; Edom refused passage (20:18–21).
“You shall not abhor an אֲדֹמִי, for he is your brother.”
David put garrisons in all Edom, “and all Edom became servants to David”.
“Who is this coming from אֱדוֹם, with crimsoned garments from Bozrah? … Why is your clothing אָדֹם?”: the prophet plays the name against the word it comes from.
“Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? Yet I loved Jacob, and Esau I hated”, said of Edom the nation; quoted Rom 9:13.
Esau, “who for one meal sold his birthright”: the act the name recalls.
“That they may possess the remnant of אֱדוֹם, and all the nations over whom my name is called”; James quotes it as “the rest of men” (Act 15:17), reading the consonants as אָדָם.
Ἰδουμαία, the land’s name in Greek dress; the Peshitta writes אַדוּם.
“(Heb. אֱדוֹם) … in LXX … elsewhere, as Ge 25:30, Ἐδώμ”.

evidence.locator: Gen.25.30, אֱדוֹם → εδωμ; הָאָדֹם → πυρροῦ; Gen.36.1 → εδωμ; Oba.1.8 → ιδουμαίας

note: Takes a.bd.af (the name, 102 tokens, nearly all the nation and land; one is the second half of עֹבֵד אֱדוֹם at 2Sa 6:10, which belongs to Obed-edom). The gentilic אֲדֹמִי (a.bd.ag) is now a word in adam.json. The only person record bearing אֱדוֹם is Esau@Gen.25.25; the land and people are a place record and are not tagged. No `word`: the name is not pointed as any word of the root entry (אָדֹם “red” with the vowels of a name). Scripture gives the name one reason, the red stew (Gen 25:30); the red birth (25:25) explains nothing in the text but uses a word of the same root, and the summary keeps the two apart. An Esau name entry (עֵשָׂו, root of its own) is not drafted here. Leads not followed: Akkadian Udūmu and Egyptian jdwmꜥ for the land (Wiktionary only; the TLA lemma was not found); Edomite ʾdm on seals; the element Edom in Obed-edom, which Krahmalkov p. 33 compares with a Phoenician divine name ʾdm.
